story.title: 1857 की रहस्यमयी रोटियाँ
story.topic: The 1857 'chapati movement': chapatis passed village to village across north India months before the uprising; origin and purpose never established
story.angle: Rotis raced from village to village across north India months before 1857, nobody ever found out who started it or why, and the competing theories (revolt signal vs cholera charm) are still open
story.centralQuestion: इन रोटियों को कौन भेज रहा था, और क्यों?
story.audience: Indian Shorts viewers 18-35, history-curious, not specialists
story.coreEmotion: uneasy curiosity turning into honest not-knowing
story.takeaway: A spooky coincidence is not proof: the best evidence points to a cholera charm, but nobody can say for sure, and the link to the revolt is unproven
story.sensitivity: 1857 is a freedom-struggle event with strong feelings: do not belittle the uprising or claim the chapatis caused it; present British suspicion as suspicion; rural people and the Delhi court shown with dignity; cholera charm described, not mocked

claims.claim: At the end of January 1857 Mark Thornhill, magistrate at Mathura (Muttra), found four small cakes of coarse flour on his office table; a man had given one cake to a village watchman (chowkidar) with orders to bake four like it and give them to the watchmen of the adjacent villages, who were to do the same.

sources.title: Mark Thornhill, The Personal Adventures and Experiences of a Magistrate during the Rise, Progress and Suppression of the Indian Mutiny (London, 1884), ch. I, pp. 2-3 (Internet Archive full text)
sources.quote: It was at the end of January 1857 ... I found four little cakes laid on the table, dirty little cakes of the coarsest flour ... A man had come to a village, and given a cake to the watchman, with injunctions to bake four like it, to distribute them to the watchmen of the adjacent villages, and to desire them to do the same.

sources.title: Mike Dash, 'The chupatty movement' (A Blast From The Past, 2010; author of the Smithsonian article 'Pass it on'), citing Thornhill, Kaye, Hibbert, Ireland and Kim A. Wagner, The Great Fear of 1857 (2010)
sources.quote: four 'dirty little cakes of the coarsest flour, about the size and thickness of a biscuit'

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Mark Thornhill'

claims.qualification: say मथुरा के मजिस्ट्रेट; 'four' is Thornhill's number (other accounts give other numbers)
claims.notes: Dash dates it 'early February'; Thornhill's own text says end of January 1857. Narration gives no month for this scene.

claims.claim: The cakes were being distributed the same way over all 'Upper India' (north India) in early 1857; popular accounts say from the Narmada to the Nepal border.

claims.claim: Hakim Ahsanullah, confidential physician to the King of Delhi (Bahadur Shah Zafar), stated: 'Nobody can tell what was the object of the distribution of the chupatties. It is not known who first projected the plan. All the people in the palace wondered what it could mean.'

claims.claim: Many contemporaries read the chapatis as a signal or warning of a coming outbreak ('a kind of fiery cross, to call them to action'; 'a forerunner of some universal popular outbreak'); Collector Ford of Gurgaon reported 'a signal' whose purport had not transpired.

claims.claim: Another contemporary reading was a charm against disease: cholera had ravaged several districts the previous autumn, and a custom of passing on objects to carry off sickness was reported.

options.text: रातों-रात, एक गाँव से दूसरे गाँव पहुँचती रोटियाँ।
options.critique: strangest image first, 8 words, no background; opens 'who/why' without answering; loops with the last line

options.text: अठारह सौ सत्तावन में अंग्रेज़ों को सबसे ज़्यादा डर किससे था? रोटियों से।
options.critique: punchy but 'सबसे ज़्यादा' is an unsupported superlative; question-answer opener feels like a quiz

options.text: मथुरा के मजिस्ट्रेट की मेज़ पर, चार रोटियाँ रखी थीं।
options.critique: specific and true, count moment, but needs a beat to explain why that is strange

options.text: एक रोटी, जिसमें कोई ख़त नहीं था, फिर भी पूरी अंग्रेज़ी हुकूमत डर गई।
options.critique: overstates ('पूरी हुकूमत डर गई'); gives away the 'no letter' beat

options.text: बग़ावत से कुछ महीने पहले, उत्तर भारत में एक अजीब चेन चल रही थी।

hooks.reason: Image-first and true (C17 qualified as 'overnight'); the open question lands at ~4 s; the ending line repeats the hook image so the Short loops; H3 is reused as the count beat at ~7 s.

weaknesses.issue: 159 words: rhythm.py estimates 59.7 s at its default rate, but at Jessica's measured 2.45 words/s the speech runs ~66 s and the video ~69 s, above the 60-65 s aim. If words.json confirms >65 s after tighten_pauses, cut 'जवाब आज भी नहीं।' (-4 words) and 'दिल्ली के' (-2)

The 100-200 miles a night estimate (C05) and Wagner's Indore/cholera conclusion (C10) are known only through Mike Dash's page-cited blog and a popular article; Wagner's book and the Smithsonian article (403) were not opened. Both are spoken with qualifiers ('एक अफ़सर का अंदाज़ा', 'मानते हैं ... शायद')
'रातों-रात' means 'overnight / very fast'; sources give a per-night rate, not proof that runners moved only at night. Visual uses dusk (no night preset), which matches the honest reading
1 new set (village) + 2 adapted (office, cantonment) + globe reuse; roti card art, night preset, carry pose and India globe dots are future development before render

S2 'और अंग्रेज़ परेशान, इन्हें भेज कौन रहा है?' is elliptical spoken Hindi; a voice artist may want 'अंग्रेज़ परेशान थे'. 'टोटका' could sound dismissive; kept because it is the everyday word and the line is framed as what others said
Intensity is moderate throughout (peak 5.5 lexical); the Meerut flash and the score carry the turn more than the wording

publishing.description:
1857 की शुरुआत में उत्तर भारत में गाँव-गाँव चपातियाँ पहुँच रही थीं। मथुरा के मजिस्ट्रेट मार्क थॉर्नहिल ने लिखा कि एक आदमी ने चौकीदार को एक रोटी दी और कहा, ऐसी चार बनाकर आसपास के गाँवों के चौकीदारों को दो। जाँच हुई, पर ये पता नहीं चला कि इसे किसने शुरू किया, कहाँ से, या क्यों। आगरा के एक अधिकारी (George Harvey) का अंदाज़ा था कि ये एक रात में 100-200 मील बढ़ रही थीं। कुछ अफ़सरों ने इसे बग़ावत का इशारा माना, कुछ ने हैजे से बचने का टोटका; अफ़वाहें धर्म भ्रष्ट करने और लखनऊ दरबार की साज़िश की भी थीं। मई 1857 में मेरठ से बग़ावत शुरू हुई। इतिहासकार Kim A. Wagner के मुताबिक ये शायद इंदौर से हैजे को भगाने की कोशिश के रूप में शुरू हुआ; बग़ावत से इसका कोई रिश्ता साबित नहीं हुआ।
Sources: Mark Thornhill, Personal Adventures and Experiences of a Magistrate (1884), pp. 2-3 (https://archive.org/details/personaladventur00thor); J. W. Kaye, A History of the Sepoy War in India, vol. I, incl. appendix statements (https://archive.org/details/cu31924021098441); Mike Dash, 'The chupatty movement' (https://mikedashhistory.com/2010/09/07/the-chupatty-movement/), citing Kim A. Wagner, The Great Fear of 1857 (Peter Lang, 2010); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Meerut'.
publishing.pinnedComment: एक बात जो वीडियो में नहीं आ पाई: अवध के एक बयान के मुताबिक वहाँ चौकीदार को दो रोटियाँ मिलीं, और हुक्म था दस और बनाकर पाँच पास के चौकीदारों को दो-दो देने का। यानी हर इलाक़े में गिनती अलग थी। मार्च 1857 में एक अंग्रेज़ डॉक्टर, Gilbert Hadow, ने अपनी बहन को लिखा: 'पूरे भारत में एक बहुत रहस्यमयी चीज़ चल रही है।' आपको क्या लगता है, रोटियाँ इशारा थीं, या दुआ?
